📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

According to recent reports, wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

According to recent reports, feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:.

Caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

In a recent development, chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future looks feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

Industry observers note that if imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love prepares a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

Sources indicate that no respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

Industry observers note that if they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

Industry observers note that if your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

Breaking: Robert Pattinson as James Bond indicates a lot about Amazon's aims for 007

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Creativebloq

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as rumours about the casting of the next James Bond began to hot up this week, my phone has been busy.
  • So you can imagine my surprise when Robert Pattinson was indeed announced as the upcoming James Bond this afternoon.
  • According to recent reports, it perhaps isn't surprising that Blofeld's—sorry, Bezos's—tech giant has opted for such a bankable star.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as rumours about the casting of the next James Bond began to hot up this week, my phone has been busy. Most of my friends (hello, both!) know me as a huge James Bond fan, and have wanted to know who I thought was going to get the role. Well, one thing's for sure, I told them all. It won't be Pattinson. Mark my words. He's just too famous.

So you can imagine my surprise when Robert Pattinson was indeed announced as the upcoming James Bond this afternoon. Everything about the news feels bizarre to me, including the lack of press release and associated fanfare (whereas Daniel Craig rode down the Thames on a speedboat, Pattinson was announced via a simple social media post). But the biggest shock is that Pattinson is by far the most famous person to be cast in the role. He's the first bonafide A-lister to pick up the Walther PPK. He's Batman, for God's sake. For better or worse, the Bond brand changed forever today. And it's thanks to one name: Amazon.

According to recent reports, it perhaps isn't surprising that Blofeld's—sorry, Bezos's—tech giant has opted for such a bankable star. The company paid billions to acquire MGM (which owned the rights to Bond), and will want a return on its investment. But the whole thing seems so at odds with the ethos of the previous Bond custodians. "I felt I had to have an unknown actor, not a star," producer Cubby Broccoli remarked of the search for the very first Bond. "Above all, a man you’d believe could be James Bond.".

It has been revealed that for decades, Bond has been one of the most carefully controlled brands in entertainment. The gun barrel sequence, the theme tune, the 007 logo, the Aston Martin; every element is instantly recognisable, and has been meticulously protected by the Broccoli family. Bond films have always felt like events, partly because they don't come along very often. But Amazon doesn't do scarcity, it does content. And with the tech giant now in creative control of the franchise, it's hard not to wonder how long it will be before 007 becomes less of a cinematic institution and more of an endlessly expandable IP. I'm not sure I'm ready for the 'Young Q' spin-off.

There are, of course, opportunities here. Bond has arguably been in need of a shake-up for some time, and Pattinson is a genuinely exciting actor, capable of bringing something strange, unpredictable and perhaps even uncomfortable to a character that has occasionally felt trapped by his own iconography. But the choice also feels like a statement of intent from Amazon. Where previous Bond actors were largely blank canvases onto which the 007 identity could be projected, Pattinson arrives with a huge, established brand of his own. Rather than making a star out of Bond, Amazon has bought a star to sell Bond. It's a subtle distinction, but a significant one. Am I going to be able to look up at the screen and see James Bond, rather than Robert Pattinson in a suit?

According to recent reports, but while it'll be Pattinson's name that hogs the headlines, the bigger question isn't simply what kind of Bond Pattinson will be, but what kind of brand Amazon wants Bond to become. Will the organization recognise that Bond's enduring appeal lies partly in his exclusivity, his mystique, and his ability to remain just a little out of reach? For all of his reinventions, 007 has always felt bigger than the actor playing him. Until today.

Daniel John is Design Editor at Creative Bloq. He reports on the worlds of design, branding and lifestyle tech, and has covered several industry events including Milan Design Week, OFFF Barcelona and Adobe Max in Los Angeles. He has interviewed leaders and designers at brands including Apple, Microsoft and Adobe. Daniel's debut book of short stories and poems was published in 2018, and his comedy newsletter is a Substack Bestseller.

  • A 12-metre-high pavilion shaped like a wedding cake is set to be dismantled at Waddesdon Manor in Buckinghamshire, UK, after it was closed over health and safety concerns.
  • A spokesperson for the Grade I-listed country house told the BBC that the pavilion, which was installed in 2023, was not “open for quite as long as hoped” due to faults in its ceramic tiles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Chris Lacey and Merriman Photography.

A 12-metre-high pavilion shaped like a wedding cake is set to be dismantled at Waddesdon Manor in Buckinghamshire, UK, after it was closed over health and safety concerns.

A spokesperson for the Grade I-listed country house told the BBC that the pavilion, which was installed in 2023, was not “open for quite as long as hoped” due to faults in its ceramic tiles.

The sculptural pavilion, simply named Wedding Cake, was designed by Portuguese artist Joana Vasconcelos as a permanent garden pavilion for the grounds of Waddesdon Manor.

Its three tiers are wrapped in glazed, pastel-toned ceramic tiles made by the historic Portuguese tile manufacturer Viúva Lamego and intended to look like cake icing. They are now faulty, forcing the structure to close because of concerns about their safety.

A report including photos of the damaged tiles was shared on Buckinghamshire Council’s online planning portal, but the root cause has not been publicly stated.

According to the BBC, a Buckinghamshire Council officer found that no viable solution to repair the faulty tiles had been identified.

As such, the council has approved a change to the listed building consent, allowing the sculpture to be removed. As the manor and its grounds are protected sites, permission must be obtained to carry out such work.

According to recent reports, the structure must now be removed no later than January 2036. However, the Rothschild Foundation, which manages the estate, wants the sculpture removed as soon as possible, according to the BBC.

The revised consent also requires the surrounding landscape to be returned to grass within six months of its removal.

When the pavilion was completed, its designer Vasconcelos told Dezeen it was her “most ambitious project to date”.

Her use of tiles reflected her ambition to use ceramics and textiles to challenge traditional hierarchies of what she called “noble materials”, such as marble, in grand architectural settings.

The manufacturer Viúva Lamego’s standard 14-by-14 centimetre tiles determined the size of the overall structure. It has an 11-metre diameter, which was the smallest that could be achieved using the tiles.

The pavilion is the fourth project by Vasconcelos created for the estate, which was built in the 1870s by Baron Ferdinand de Rothschild to entertain guests and showcase his ceramic collections.

A spokesperson for the manor noted it intends to continue to commission artwork for its grounds.

“We are hoping to continue to showcase art in the landscape, including looks for a newly introduced contemporary sculpture trail in the grounds of Waddesdon Manor, which will open in July 2027,” they said.

Other projects by Vasconcelos featured on Dezeen include a 24-metre-long textile installation for Dior’s Autumn Winter 2023 catwalk show.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, we recently reported on the dismantling of Rike Concert Hall, designed by Italian practice Studio Fuksas. It is being demolished less than 15 years after it was completed, and before ever opening to the public.

Photography by Chris Lacey and Merriman Photography.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago has received a promised gift of 65 artworks from longtime supporters Jack and Sandra Guthman to mark its 60th anniversary.

Sources indicate that the gift from the Chicago-based collectors spans paintings, photography, works on paper, and sculptures, and includes works by Pope.L, Gary Simmons, Andrea Bowers, Christian Marclay, Elle Pérez, and Shinique Smith. The museum mentioned in a release that the selected works were chosen in tandem with the curatorial staff, “taking the MCA’s collecting priorities into serious consideration.” Related Articles Bluhm Family Gives $5 M. to MCA Chicago for Gender Equity Fund, Named After Outgoing Director Outgoing MCA Chicago Director Madeleine Grynsztejn Offers the Consummate Insider's Guide to the Windy City.

Industry observers note that in its announcement, the MCA Chicago reported that, of the 54 artists represented in the gift, 23 (or 43 percent) are people of color, 19 (or 35 percente) are women, and 13 are entering the collection for the first time, among them Rashid Johnson, Christopher Wool, Dawoud Bey, and Amanda Williams. Johnson’s traveling survey, which opened at the Guggenheim Museum last year, is currently on view at the MCA Chicago; Williams will have a solo show at the museum next year.

Sources indicate that “Together, Jack and Sandy have helped shape Chicago’s cultural life through their collecting, advocacy, and longstanding engagement with artists and institutions,” MCA Chicago director Madeleine Grynsztejn remarked in a statement. “To be entrusted with this tremendous gift is a great honor.”.

The Guthmans first donated an artwork to the museum in 1988, and Jack joined the board of trustees the year after. To mark its 50th anniversary in 2016, they donated work by 50 women-identifying photographers, which was the subject of the exhibition “Woman With a Camera.” With the newly donated 65 works, the Guthmans have given a total of 130 works over the past nearly four decades, the largest amount by a single collector in the MCA Chicago’s history.

Jack is an attorney who has worked on several mega-developments in Chicago. He is also the founder and past board chair of the Chicago Architecture Biennial. Sandra worked at IBM from 1965 to 1993, rising from systems engineer to director of marketing for the Midwest. She also served as chief executive and chair of the Chicago-based Polk Bros. Foundation; she is now chair emerita. In addition to the MCA Chicago, they have supported the Art Institute of Chicago, the Hyde Park Art Center, Theaster Gates’s Art Bank, and the Harris Theater for Music and Dance. At the Harris, they sponsored the creation of the Guthman Gallery.

Recent findings suggest that last month, the MCA Chicago received a $5 million gift from the Bluhm family to endow the Women Artists Initiative, which will provide funds in perpetuity to help the museum achieve its gender equity goals in its programming and collection. Both gifts are meant to honor Grynsztejn, who is stepping down at the end of the year.

According to recent reports, “We are fortunate to have the opportunity to donate these works as the MCA marks its 60th anniversary and as Madeleine Grynsztejn steps down after a remarkable tenure as its Pritzker Director,” the Guthmans stated in a statement. “We celebrate both the institution and the woman who has lifted it to a where it is today—a Chicago institution now acknowledged as a leader in the world of contemporary art.”.

Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1295 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears.
  • Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort.
  • In a recent development, clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation. Takeaway Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies. PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

EMBT shelters Naples metro station beneath "natural and welcoming" vaulted timber roof

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spanish architecture studio EMBT has completed the Naples Underground Central Station in Italy, contrasting its modernist surroundings with a wavy timber roof.
  • The station, which is shortlisted in the Infrastructure and transport category of Dezeen Awards 2026, sits within the Centro Direzionale, a business district in Naples designed in the 1970s by Japanese architect Kenzo Tange.
  • The 10,000-square-metre building was designed to replace a previously understated metro entrance with a new public plaza that felt more integrated with the surrounding city.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Roland Halbe.

Spanish architecture studio EMBT has completed the Naples Underground Central Station in Italy, contrasting its modernist surroundings with a wavy timber roof.

The station, which is shortlisted in the Infrastructure and transport category of Dezeen Awards 2026, sits within the Centro Direzionale, a business district in Naples designed in the 1970s by Japanese architect Kenzo Tange.

The 10,000-square-metre building was designed to replace a previously understated metro entrance with a new public plaza that felt more integrated with the surrounding city.

As EMBT founder Benedetta Tagliabue previously told Dezeen during the station’s construction, the curvilinear timber canopy was designed in direct response to what she called the “artificial” feel of the modernist Centro Direzionale.

“Kenzo Tange designed Centro Direzionale, and he built a very Kenzo Tange-type of city with reflective skyscrapers and a piazza, very 1970s, very clean,” she told Dezeen in 2021.

It has been revealed that “It didn’t work because it’s so different from the rest of Naples,” Tagliabue continued. “So the idea of making a newly introduced station there and connecting with the new subway line was also to try to introduce a piece of nature and a piece of the original part of Naples into this artificial piece of the city.”.

The roof of the station was constructed from arches and beams of glue-laminated (glulam) timber, which are partially supported by the existing concrete structure and shelter a floor finished in local Etna and Trani limestone.

According to Tagliabue, the branching columns and supports of these arches were designed to evoke the feeling of “walking through a forest”, while referencing the arched roofs of historic railway stations.

“We wanted the everyday experience of catching a train to feel more natural and welcoming, giving people a sense of being at home in the middle of the city,” she told Dezeen.

“We were also interested in what wood could bring to this particular neighbourhood. There is so much glass and concrete here; introducing timber was a way of bringing back a connection with nature, through its warmth and texture,” she added.

“The roof follows the geometry of the tracks, so something that is normally hidden underground becomes visible in the shape of the building.”.

The vaulted canopy not only shelters the station’s ticket barriers and access routes, but extends towards the new surrounding paved plaza on either side, which faces a church to the north and incorporates new planting to the south.

Sources indicate that below ground, the station platforms are lined entirely with striped panels in bold shades of red, orange and yellow informed by Pompeian frescoes. This theme is continued above ground in the form of colourful silhouettes.

Industry observers note that “Our station is not directly above archaeological remains, so we introduced our own references to that history, with a little humour. The reds and yellows recall Pompeii, and figures appear and disappear across the surfaces,” Tagliabue explained.

“I like the idea that a station can offer these unexpected encounters: along the way, you discover something about the city and feel more connected to it,” she added.

Elsewhere in Naples, sculptor Anish Kapoor and architecture studio AL_A previously designed two sculptural station entrances – one in weathered steel and the other in aluminium – as part of a project to connect the underground to the city’s Traiano district.

Other metro station architecture recently featured on Dezeen includes the mirrored Qasr AlHokm Metro Station in Saudi Arabia by Snøhetta and the series of buildings created for Melbourne’s Metro Tunnel by studios RSHP, Hassell and WW+P Architects.

Photography by Roland Halbe.

For Abi Palmer, Chronic Illness Is Like Being an Indoor Cat

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Artnews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “I have been trying so hard to capture the smell of rain for you,” an unseen narrator with a British accent explains in Abi Palmer Invents the Weather (2023), as cats slink across the screen.
  • This non-god, the artist Abi Palmer, is recreating the weather for her two indoor cats, mixing rainwater with moss and earth.
  • As it happens, Palmer got her start making art in the form of wet white wads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I have been trying so hard to capture the smell of rain for you,” an unseen narrator with a British accent explains in Abi Palmer Invents the Weather (2023), as cats slink across the screen. “But being as I am no god or scientist,” the voice continues, as human hands wring out a cloth soaking in a jar of dirty water, “I am forced to work backward.” Soon, dripping white fabric is seen hanging from twine inside a cardboard box, clumped like a cloud.

This non-god, the artist Abi Palmer, is recreating the weather for her two indoor cats, mixing rainwater with moss and earth. All the while, she muses on how chronic illness keeps her inside, catlike, yet also binds her intricately to meteorological variation. Palmer alludes to the ways joint pain can flare when pressure drops or smoky skies are felt by some in the lungs or in the back of the throat. Related Articles Rashid Johnson, Christopher Wool, and Dawoud Bey Enter MCA Chicago Through 65-Work Gift Artsy and Artnet Acquire First Thursday as Art-Tech Expansion Picks Up Speed.

As it happens, Palmer got her start making art in the form of wet white wads. As an “unsupervised child,” as she told me from her London apartment, she’d combine water and tissue into globby sculptures—“blob creatures”—then let them dry. Recently, making massive slug sculptures inspired by the way the species survives by ugliness, she realized how consistent her materials and methods remained. At the University of Cambridge, she studied literature, as is evident in her voice-overs and her two books: Sanitorium (2020) and Slugs: A Manifesto (2024). But soon, she found her hands hurt too much to type—though her muscles were “really bendy” and thus “good at squeezing things into quite unusual shapes,” as she had intuited at a very young age.

Sources indicate that it’s not so common, Palmer told me, for cats to live indoors in the UK: Some pet people even consider keeping them inside cruel. But her housing and health situations didn’t allow for her animals to roam freely, never mind that domestic cats kill billions of birds each year. So her video was born of a bit of guilt, an attempt at “navigating the imperfection of the world, but also the magic and beauty of it.” She admitted: “It’s absurd.”.

According to recent reports, for Palmer, retaining a childlike sense of play is essential. She came to art with little technical training. As she started to receive institutional recognition and awards—she’s been in group reveals at the National Museum of Contemporary Art (EMST) in Athens, Goldsmiths in London, EMAP in Seoul, and elsewhere, in addition to receiving the 2025 Heny Moore Foundation Award—she was struck by the haunting sense that she ought to be doing things more “properly.” But she realized: “The moment I start taking things too seriously, it’s a trap.” The external rewards come and go, often without much in the way of remuneration—so it helps to have fun with art. “I take play very seriously,” Palmer said.

Her work attests: In Abi Palmer Invents the Weather she not only elaborately simulates meteorological conditions but highlights the video within playful cardboard constructions that she reconfigures for each exhibition: a feline paradise. In a world that tends to address disability and illness in the gravest of tones, Palmer infuses humor. For disabled people, humor can be a survival tactic, a way of putting others at ease with difference—often, not without some resentment. But it is also simply true that life is never one-note.

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Sources indicate that tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

In a recent development, these tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Sources indicate that tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Recent findings suggest that fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

According to recent reports, tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Sources indicate that flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

In a recent development, furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Engineering company Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid building with mass-timber elements that the company claims is the tallest of its type in Brazil.
  • Standing 22 metres tall, Aurora 275 is considered a hybrid-timber building, with a structural system consisting of a reinforced concrete core, metal, and mass-timber elements including glued-laminated timber (glulam) beams and columns.
  • Located in the Suzano area of São Paulo, according to Crosslam, it is the tallest building of its type in Brazil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Helio Leite.

Engineering company Crosslam has designed and built Aurora 275, a hybrid building with mass-timber elements that the company claims is the tallest of its type in Brazil.

Standing 22 metres tall, Aurora 275 is considered a hybrid-timber building, with a structural system consisting of a reinforced concrete core, metal, and mass-timber elements including glued-laminated timber (glulam) beams and columns.

Located in the Suzano area of São Paulo, according to Crosslam, it is the tallest building of its type in Brazil.

Crosslam, which usually acts as an engineer for other firms, designed the building itself to demonstrate the potential of mass timber in Brazil.

It has been revealed that “We believed that, to sell the first timber building, we first had to build our own,” mentioned Crosslam founder José Alberto Corrêa. “Otherwise, the Brazilian market wouldn’t trust that it was possible.”.

Recent findings suggest that to further demonstrate the method’s viability, the building was constructed in four weeks by a five-person team, according to Crosslam. The timber was produced in the manufacturer’s factory using wood sourced from Brazil.

Aurora 275 sits next to smaller residential buildings. It features a metal-clad facade, with yellow detailing running up its face.

It extends in two directions from a concrete core, with balconies for each of the 10 apartments.

On the outside, the timber elements are only visible on the undersides of the balconies.

However, on the inside, the timber elements are more visible, with the cross-laminated timber floorplates and glulam beams exposed, giving the interiors a warm feel.

Crosslam mentioned that the structure shows the potential for timber buildings for industrial-style housing production in the country.

“Using engineered timber offers benefits related to the industrialisation of construction, the efficiency of the assembly process, and building performance,” remarked the project teaam.

“The main advantages include: faster assembly, dimensional precision, reduced waste on the construction site, a lighter structure, and lower carbon emissions.”.

The company claimed that the building is carbon neutral.

Timber construction for tall buildings is gaining popularity across the world, with inroads into construction in North America and Europe. The current tallest timber structure in the world recently topped out in Australia.

Photography by Helio Leite.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's already a lot of competition among the best laser cutters and engravers for crafters, and Creality makes the best budget pick in our guide with its Falcon A1. Today, it's thrown a new contender into the mix, and it looks like it could be a game changer for small personalisation businesses and crafters who want to work remotely.

The next-gen Creality Falcon T1C promises high-performance customisation capabilities, but it's also impressively compact, making it versatile and convenient for things like making custom gifts or adding names, photos, custom text or unique designs to everyday products on location at craft markets and other events (also see our guide to the best 3D printers).

The Falcon T1C is built has a dual-laser configuration that makes it compatible with a wide range of materials. A 15W blue diode laser can process wood, bamboo, leather and dark acrylic, while a 5.5W infrared laser is designed for precision metal marking, dark acrylics and a range of synthetic materials.

Creality says the machine's galvanometer setup (the system that uses motorised mirrors to steer a laser beam) is capable of very fast scan speeds of up to 6,500 mm/s in specified image engraving modes. Using the company's PixelFlow control technology, the system coordinates galvo movement and laser power to preserve fine grayscale details while boosting image-processing efficiency by up to 8x compared to conventional processing under laboratory conditions.

Ultra-fine laser spot sizes (as small as 0.06 x 0.05 mm for the blue diode and 0.03 x 0.03 mm for the infrared laser) promise accurate reproduction for delicate lines, including intricate textures and tiny text, making it possible to personalise very small items.

Industry observers note that aside from the focus on precision, In think what really makes the Falcon T1C a potential game changer is its compact footprint. This makes it an appealing choice for small home studios and workshops but also for anyone who wants to take their customisation business on the move to pop-up event markets. This compactness doesn't necessarily mean sacrificing on potential project size either. The standard 120 x 120 mm working area can be expanded to 120 x 480mm with an optional extension bed for larger items.

One-touch autofocus and camera-assisted positioning should be helpful for speeding up workflows, while the Falcon Design Space software's preset layers eliminate the need to physically swap laser modules or re-align positions, again increasing efficiency for working remotely. It also provides AI Outline Tracing, AI Background Removal, Smart Fill, and AI Filters—to rapidly transform design concepts into production-ready physical goods.

An expanded engraving cloud includes MakerMuse and CraftSeek, which provide users with access to an extensive digital design library, cloud storage and collaborative tools to streamline design preparation and manage projects.

But what about price? Pre-orders for the Creality Falcon T1C opened today ahead of a commercial release in mid-December 2026. In the US, the Standalone Edition has an MSRP of $1,699, but if you reserve today with a $50 deposit, you can save $500 reducing the pre-order price to $1,199.

According to recent reports, A Combo Edition including the AP1S Air Purifier has an MSRP of $1,859. Preorder with a $60 reservation to receive $600 in savings, bringing the price down to $1,259.

To pre-order, visit the Creality US store.

Latest Update: Sotheby’s, Blaquier-Arrieta Family Reach Deal With Fischer Heirs, Clearing Way for $180 M. Van Gogh Sale

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sotheby’s has reached an agreement with the heirs of a Jewish publisher who challenged the sale of a $180 million Vincent van Gogh painting last week, clearing the way for the picture to go under the hammer Wednesday night.
  • The auction house noted Tuesday that the Blaquier-Arrieta family, which has owned van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs (1890) since 1975, reached a settlement with all the legal descendants of Hedwig and Samuel Fischer.
  • The deal brings an end to a messy public brawl that erupted last Thursday in the pages of the New York Times, just six days before the painting was due to lead Sotheby’s $450 million sale of the Blaquier-Arrieta collection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sotheby’s has reached an agreement with the heirs of a Jewish publisher who challenged the sale of a $180 million Vincent van Gogh painting last week, clearing the way for the picture to go under the hammer Wednesday night.

The auction house noted Tuesday that the Blaquier-Arrieta family, which has owned van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs (1890) since 1975, reached a settlement with all the legal descendants of Hedwig and Samuel Fischer. The terms weren’t disclosed, but Sotheby’s confirmed to ARTnews that the agreement resolves the ownership claims and that the painting’s buyer will receive clear title. Related Articles At Sotheby's $378.7 M. Doubleheader, Buyers Take Risks Again, Even as Bidding Drags Yayoi Kusama 'Infinity Net' Painting Sells for $15.1 M. at Sotheby's, Setting a Record.

The deal brings an end to a messy public brawl that erupted last Thursday in the pages of the New York Times, just six days before the painting was due to lead Sotheby’s $450 million sale of the Blaquier-Arrieta collection.

Industry observers note that as the Times first reported, the Fischer heirs argued that their family had been forced to sell the painting in Amsterdam in 1936 because of financial pressures brought on by Nazi persecution. Their Berlin lawyer, Gunnar Schnabel, demanded Sotheby’s withdraw the work from sale unless it could establish that the transaction had been voluntary.

In a recent development, sotheby’s disputed that account. As ARTnews reported on Sunday the auction house noted records from the archives of the art dealer Paul Cassirer highlighted that the painting sold for 68,000 Swiss francs, or approximately $22,000, in June 1936. Sotheby’s maintained that this was a fair price for a van Gogh at the time, and that the picture had been in Amsterdam for nearly three years before its sale.

Industry observers note that the timing of the claim raised eyebrows among several art-market professionals who spoke to ARTnews under the condition of anonymity. Some saw it as a pressure tactic, arriving when Sotheby’s had little time to respond and plenty to lose if the picture was withdrawn. The auction house had guaranteed the work for an undisclosed sum and spent months promoting it as the star of one of the season’s biggest sales.

Judd Grossman, a New York art lawyer who isn’t involved in the dispute, warned that recent changes to the HEAR Act, which governs Nazi-era restitution claims, could encourage more of what he called “gamesmanship by claimants waiting to the very last minute to come forward before seeking their slice of the pie.” (As part of a separate ongoing lawsuit, lawyers for the Republic of Austria, the Albertina Museum, and the Leopold Museum Foundation have labeled the updated HEAR Act unconstitutional.).

Whether the Fischer heirs received any financial compensation under the agreement is unclear. Nor does the settlement establish whether the painting was sold under duress in 1936. In Tuesday’s announcement, Sotheby’s stated the agreement recognized both the painting’s complicated history and the persecution suffered by the Fischer family under the Nazis.

The Fischer heirs welcomed the settlement, thanking Sotheby’s and the Blaquier-Arrieta family for what they called a “trusting and fair negotiation” that acknowledged their family’s suffering and honored Gisela Bermann Fischer’s long history of pursuing restitution.

Industry observers note that bermann Fischer, who died in 2014, had previously pursued restitution for artworks lost by her family during the Nazi era. In 2007, she declined to oppose the sale of a Paul Cezanne work that had passed through the same Amsterdam dealer, while expressly reserving her right to challenge other sales.

The Blaquier-Arrieta family also described the settlement positively, saying in a statement it looked forward to “an extraordinary result and to passing along this masterpiece to a new generation of collectors.”.

What's Love Got to Do With It? The Relationship Cycle Explained

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

In a recent development, each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

It has been revealed that from those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:.

It has been revealed that welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

In a recent development, research shows that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

If the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of new love into a warm, enduring attachment.

Hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the issues head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

In a recent development, significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

If you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

In a recent development, you know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Sources indicate that every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

Prince George made the headlines recently by displaying his artistic flair. The second in line to the throne impressed readers of Country Life magazine last week, when his colour pencil drawing of a kingfisher appeared in a special concern guest edited by his father, the Prince of Wales.

Industry observers note that shortly afterwards, the drawing went viral and amazed audiences on social media as well. It’s not hard to see why. The bird, which is playfully perched on a little branch and looking away from the viewer, demonstrates a level of craft you might not expect to come from the hands of a 12-year-old.

It has been revealed that if you wish you could draw this well, and you’ve exhausted all of our how to draw tutorials, you might be in luck. Because shrewd online detectives may have figured out the secret behind the Prince’s handiwork.

Upon being shared on the likes of X and Instagram, people couldn’t believe how good the drawing was. Some commenters pointed out that he may have inherited his artistic talent from his family. After all, Prince George’s grandfather, King Charles, is an avid watercolour painter, and his parents both studied art at A-level. Catherine even studied history of art while at university.

The internet being what it is though, it wasn’t long until jealous users credited the drawing’s success to the amount of time and extra tuition the Prince surely enjoyed. However it seems he may have simply followed an easily accessible online course.

In amongst the comments, it soon became apparent that Prince George’s drawing bears more than a passing resemblance to the kingfisher featured in Matt Fussell’s course titled 3 Little Birds. And while no official confirmation has been made at the time of writing, everything from the pose to the positioning on the branch appears to be very similar.

This isn’t to take away from the Prince’s drawing. His picture still showcases a great level of skill and a keen understanding of the materials. In this case, if he followed the tutorial to the letter, Prince George used wax-based Prismacolor Premier Pencils on smooth Bristol paper. Both of which can be easily picked up from most local art supply shops.

Sources indicate that if anything, it should be an encouragement to aspiring artists. With the help of one course, which can be enjoyed as either videos or step-by-step written instructions, you too can start layering your colours and creating your own beautiful bird illustrations (see our how to draw a bird tutorial, for example).

According to the course outline on his website, Matt’s instructions make the drawing process easy by breaking everything down into simple lessons. These cover everything from the proportions to colour transitions, as well as texture and highlights. Follow the course through to the end, and you’ll also learn how to draw a blue jay with oil-based polychroma pencils by Faber Castell, and a hummingbird with wax-based luminance coloured-pencils from Caran D’Ache.

Sources indicate that on top of helping you draw like Prince George, these are also useful skills that can be carried over into future studies. And if you’re not happy with your results, Matt even offers a 30 day money back guarantee on his $57 course.

Industry observers note that dom Carter is a freelance writer who specialises in art and design. Formerly a staff writer for Creative Bloq, his work has also appeared on Creative Boom and in the pages of ImagineFX, Computer Arts, 3D World, and .net. Finnegan Shannon installs conveyor belt for displaying art accessibly in Brooklyn

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to Pioneer Works, the There’s No Me Without You installation fulfils Shannon’s “longtime fantasy of an exhibition space that would meet their access needs”.
  • Chairs were placed around the closed-loop 12-foot-long mechanism, letting visitors sit when viewing and engaging with exhibited objects, archival materials and portable DVD players placed on a series of moving trays.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Dan Bradica.

New York City-based artist Finnegan Shannon has installed a conveyor belt to display art at cultural centre Pioneer Works in Brooklyn, USA, as a commentary on accessibility in art.

According to Pioneer Works, the There’s No Me Without You installation fulfils Shannon’s “longtime fantasy of an exhibition space that would meet their access needs”.

Chairs were placed around the closed-loop 12-foot-long mechanism, letting visitors sit when viewing and engaging with exhibited objects, archival materials and portable DVD players placed on a series of moving trays.

It was created from a restaurant-style system similar to those used in sushi restaurants where the food is delivered via a conveyor belt. The rest of the room on the upper floor of the arts centre was covered in rich fabrics and built-in benches along the perimeter.

“My conveyor belt, technically a retail and restaurant-style display system, is a tool for me to be in less pain when I’m experiencing art,” remarked Shannon, who is disabled. “I notice I am a much more patient and curious visitor when I’m sitting down.”.

The title of the installation reflects the artist’s relationship to the concept of interdependence.

“If disabled people were in charge, we would have a bunch of varied and deluxe options for sitting and lying down in exhibition spaces,” they mentioned.

“Instead we live in a world where this type of infrastructure is quite basic and sparse.”.

The installation is being used to present new commissions by artists with disabilities Joselia Rebekah Hughes, Ariana Martinez and Alex Dolores Salerno. For the three consecutive exhibitions, visitors are invited to interact with the work through touch, sight, and sound.

Air filters with bright colours were included in the middle of the conveyor belt to assist with air quality and masks were encouraged for visitors.

Shannon emphasised the collaborative nature of artistic endeavour through the exhibition.

“We know that on some fundamental level, no solo exhibition is truly a solo endeavor,” Shannon stated.

“Putting together an exhibition takes immense collaboration and support – art handlers, facilities staff, curators, registrars, accountants, assistants – and that is all within the institution.”.

“You can trace that entanglement further: I’m dependent on workers, paid and unpaid care labor, and friendships, family, and more, both locally and across the globe.”.

“I never want someone to come away from an exhibition with my work feeling like they’ve experienced something that is mine,” they said. “Instead I hope they have threads to follow to learn more about the vast world of knowledge that is disability culture.”.

In a recent development, shannon’s other projects have focused on access. Alt Text as Poetry, a collaboration with Bojana Coklyat exploring image description and Do You Want Us Here or Not is a series of museum benches and cushions designed to encourage rest.

Other designs that prioritise accessibility were showcased at The Fashion Institute of Technology’s Adapt/Evolve exhibition in New York last year.

There’s No Me Without You is on show at Pioneer Works in Brooklyn from 12 September to 20 December. For more exhibitions, installations and talks worldwide, visit Dezeen Events Guide.

Disney’s radical fresh animation technique will make Hexed the end of an era

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it's clear that some people are getting tired of the contemporary Disney style.
  • The fatigue was evident at D23 this year.
  • A lot of fans will be happy then to learn that Clay won't be a one off but rather the start of a whole latest Disney era after Hexed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's clear that some people are getting tired of the contemporary Disney style. That can be seen in the allegations of Disney same-face syndrome, the disappointment that Hexed doesn't look like its concept art and the perennial controversy over the hybrid live-action remakes, with Moana being the latest flop.

The fatigue was evident at D23 this year. The announcements that generated the most excitement were a return of 2D animation, if only in combination with live action for the nostalgia-heavy TV series in Oswald, and the news that Disney's Clay will look like claymation even if uses CG.

A lot of fans will be happy then to learn that Clay won't be a one off but rather the start of a whole latest Disney era after Hexed. The studio's developed a new animation pipeline that will allow it to apply different art styles to 3D models, potentially replacing the realism popularised by Pixar with a unique look for each new movie – and it's all starting with Lilo & Scratch.

It has been revealed that set to show in cinemas alongside Hexed, Lilo & Scratch is the first theatrical short from Walt Disney Animation Studios in five years. Written and directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Malcon Pierce, it will see the much-loved blue alien Stitch having to contend with the introduction of a mischievous cat called Scratch. Maia Kealoha voices Lilo, reprising her role from the 2025 live-action film Lilo & Stitch, and Chris Sanders with voice Stitch again.

Like all of the studios' feature animations in the last 15 years, the short was made using computer-generated animation with 3D models, but these are blended with hand-drawn elements to create a hybrid style that looks surprisingly faithful to Lilo & Stitch from 2002.

Disney's VFX supervisor Jeremy Sikorski has noted that the upcoming pipeline was developed through experimentation on the previous shorts Paperman and Once Upon a Studio. Pixar is also exploring the same direction, as we saw in the Gatto trailer: environments, characters and sets are modeled and animated in 3D to retain spatial depth, lighting and camera movement, but certain characters and other details are hand drawn.

Disney notes about 25% of the backgrounds in Lilo & Scratch are watercolour paintings reused from the original Lilo & Stitch, while more than a dozen newly introduced background paintings were created by artists including Tia Kratter and Larry Wu. Some of these were digitally painted in Photoshop to look like watercolour, while others were hand-painted on paper.

Combined with digital backgrounds and set extension, this blend of old and new hand-painted watercolours helped the filmmakers remain faithful to the look of the 2002 feature, Disney states.

It has been revealed that in an interview at the Governors Awards in LA on Sunday (see the post by Deadline below), Disney Animation Chief Creative Officer Jared Bush confirmed that all original Disney movies from Clay onwards will use this approach. That doesn't mean that they'll all look like Renaissance-era 2D animation, but that each with have its own "wildly different" look.

Zootopia 3 and Frozen 3 will still look like we would expect, but Hexed may be "the last original in the Disney art style as people know it," he says.

Jared Bush shares updates on ‘Zootopia 3,’ ‘Frozen 3’ and ‘Hexed’ and reveals the fresh, upcoming animated films at Disney will have “wildly different art styles”: “We’re really going to be pushing into some new areas” | #GovernorsAwards https://t.co/nw16Ci8WoDNovember 16, 2026.

It has been revealed that the new approach looks like a win for Disney. Despite some success with the live-action The Jungle Book and last year's Lilo & Stitch, the poor reception of Moana, Snow White and Mulan suggests waning interest in the remake formula is waning. Meanwhile, the 3D animation style that once looked so modern is starting to feel dated and generic.

Sources indicate that nostalgic audiences miss 2D animation, while younger audiences want something fresh. It sounds like Disney's new animation pipeline could make both things possible without sacrificing the efficiency that comes with 3D-based CG animation, which makes it much quicker and easier to swap and adjust environments, characters and props compared to traditional hand-drawn 2D, where even a relatively small change might mean having to redraw from scratch.The Disney principles of animation will remain in tact, but in a vast realm new possibilities.

I do wonder though. In ten years time, will people start to feel nostalgic about the much-maligned 3D Disney style?

Hexed will be released on 25 November. Lilo & Scratch will screen before it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, vibration plates are like mini surfboards that give you a good shimmy while you’re exercising. Though you won’t find a mountain of extensive research behind them, you may be impressed by their possible benefits.

We asked a weightlifting coach to explain and show us how to add good vibrations to our workout routine.

In a recent development, these machines, which look like platforms or scales, are designed to activate something called whole-body vibration (WBV). WBV makes the body work harder by forcing it to contract muscles automatically.

Fans of WBV like to perform classic exercises on top of these machines, including:.

Research points to WBV’s ability to boost blood flow.

Weightlifting coach Jarrod Nobbe explains that vibration plates help move blood by stimulating muscle contractions through rapid vibrations.

“The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles help pump blood more efficiently throughout the body,” he indicates.

According to recent reports, as Nobbe adds, movement generally increases blood flow and core temperature, preparing the body for activity. This means vibration plates may be an excellent warm-up activity.

A 2021 study showed that WBV can be an alternative exercise for older adults, boosting the effects of strengthening exercise.

Nobbe notes this is because WBV engages muscles in a way that mimics resistance training.

“The vibrations activate and force muscles to contract and relax multiple times per second, which can lead to gains in muscle strength and endurance over time, especially when combined with specific exercises,” he indicates.

Nobbe points to some anecdotal evidence suggesting that regular use of vibration plates may help boost energy levels, possibly thanks to increased blood circulation and enhanced muscle activation.

In a recent development, “Ultimately, I stand by the idea that movement is medicine,” Nobbe indicates. “Tons of research already proves that regular physical activity boosts mood, mental health, and promotes energy levels.”.

According to recent reports, nobbe says WBV may reduce muscle soreness, stiffness, and inflammation by encouraging blood flow to the muscles. This, he explains, aids in faster recovery post-exercise or injury.

WBV has been shown to improve bone mineral density, which Nobbe points out may positively affect those at risk of osteoporosis.

“The mechanical vibrations stimulate bone cells, potentially leading to increased bone density and strength, delivering the same positive bone health benefits of resistance training,” he states.

“Unfortunately, vibration plates aren’t a one-stop shop for weight loss,” Nobbe indicates.

He explains that vibration plates alone are unlikely to significantly reduce belly fat without dietary changes and additional exercise.

“While vibration plates can contribute to overall calorie expenditure and muscle activation, targeted fat loss requires a comprehensive approach including diet, cardio exercise, and resistance training,” he says.

These tips will help you stand on your vibration plate with a slight bend at your knee or perform exercises on top of it.

More research is needed around WBV — AKA what happens when you use a vibration plate — but existing smaller research is promising.

Use your machine carefully, and remember to maintain a healthy lifestyle and workout routine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A bookshelf slots in below the cantilevered seat of Kino, a 3D-printed chair developed by Barcelona-based designer Pablo Castillo.

Castillo designed Kino for Decibel, an American firm that specialises in 3D-printed furniture and installations. It is shortlisted for seating design of the year in the upcoming Dezeen Awards.

The designer’s aim was to create a recognisable chair silhouette, while also responding to the specificities of the 3D printing process.

The chair is essentially a monobloc, with a single component forming the T-shaped seat, two legs, the shelf and a curved backrest.

Sources indicate that its entire form is printed from PLA, the most common bioplastic, although the material is reinforced with cellulose plant fibres. This increases its strength, enabling the cantilevered seat.

Decibal also offers an outdoor version printed from recycled PETG, a thermoplastic polyester.

“I wanted the substantial thickness of the plastic and the way it builds a product layer by layer to translate into features that give the chair its character,” Castillo told Dezeen.

“Following this line of thought allowed me to move beyond mere dimensions and general ergonomic considerations,” the designer remarked.

“The cantilevered seat, the under-seat storage, and specific details such as the T-junctions naturally emerged.”.

According to recent reports, the seat’s T-shape was created by cantilevers both forwards and backwards. This makes the chair less rigid than a typical 3D-printed chair, improving comfort.

“By reinforcing the lower part of the seat with a corrugated structure integrated directly into the 3D print, we achieved a chair that offers a slightly broader range of motion than a traditional design,” Castillo said.

“It seamlessly accommodates highly reclined, relaxed postures, as well as more active positions when the user leans forward.”.

Kino joins Decibel’s Editions collection, which also includes chairs by designers including Charles Birshaw, Karim Rashid and Deniz Aktay.

The Fresh Jersey-based brand launched this collection with an exhibition at the Alcova show in Milan in 2025, when it was live-printing chairs in the former SNIA factory in Varedo.

The chairs are produced using a Caracol robotic 3D printer, which allows geometries that wouldn’t be possible with injection moulding.

#22226. Are GLP-1 Drugs Quietly Changing Our Sex Lives?

📅 10 Apr 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2134 w)
